meta.title: Starship Flight 15 · Contingency · early Hawaii
about: Contingency profile: Contingency · early Hawaii. Pre-launch model: Flight 14's zone-fitted orbit with the Flight 15 timeline, a Super Heavy return and a 3-DOF entry to the Pad 2 tower; not telemetry.

Hazard areas and windows are the Flight 15 navigational warnings of 7-9 Nov 2026 (NAVAREA IV 1080/26 and 1081/26, HYDROPAC 3244, 3254, 3256 and 3257/26) and the Mexican NOTAM B4288/26 for the entry corridor.
notes: Pre-launch model, not telemetry and not an official ephemeris. Window 22:45-00:00 UTC on 13-14 Nov 2026 (16:45-18:00 CST), from the SpaceX mission page; T0 22:45 is the window open, not an announced liftoff time.

Orbit plane: Flight 14's fit to the September 2026 navigational warnings (i 30.58 deg, 275 km circular with J2 secular rates, node 2.1 deg east of the pad, the ascent steering into the plane). SpaceX: Flight 15 flies the same altitude and inclination. The orbital rate is scaled by +0.0013 (nodal period 89.629 min, as a 269 km mean orbit) so that the modeled catch happens at the official T+22:32:34; Flight 14's deorbit telemetry read 270 km against that model's 275.

Ascent: a shaped kinematic profile (Max Q 11.5 km at T+58 s, MECO 66 km and 1.5 km/s at T+2:19, SECO 150 km and 15 deg downrange at T+8:09, the Flight 14 assumptions) that ends on the suborbital coast ellipse in position and velocity. Insertion at T+26:10 is modeled at the burn start as an instantaneous circularisation at apogee.

Super Heavy: 2-D point mass from the MECO state; 36 s boostback (46 m/s^2, 1655 m/s), ballistic fall with US76 drag (ballistic coefficient 3400 kg/m^2), 25 s landing burn to rest on the Pad 2 tower, arriving from the Gulf. Apogee 102 km, 81 km maximum downrange, 634 m/s at the landing-burn start. Illustrative: the boostback and landing-burn throttles are not public.

Descents: the Starship calibrated on Flight 14's reconstructed entry (3-DOF point mass, rotating WGS-84 Earth, J2, US Standard Atmosphere 1976, modified-Newtonian belly-first aerodynamics with a 55 deg hypersonic angle of attack, L/D 0.70, ballistic coefficient 331 kg/m^2, bank steering that fades out below Mach 1.5, a 10 s one-Raptor deorbit burn). The constant bank is a model choice; SpaceX describes a series of small turns over sparsely populated areas.

Hazard areas and windows are the Flight 15 navigational warnings issued 7-9 Nov 2026 and the Mexican NOTAM B4288/26 for the return (areas C2 and C3, surface to unlimited, 2056-0014Z daily from 14 Nov: a corridor 20 to 80 km wide from the Pacific off Baja California to the Rio Grande north-west of Laredo, opening at the official entry time): NAVAREA IV 1080/26 (launch areas A and B, 2245-0040Z), NAVAREA IV 1081/26 (ship catch: Laguna Madre, Padre Island and the Gulf off Starbase, 2108-0014Z on 14-15 Nov), HYDROPAC 3244/26 (Indian Ocean, 2253-0114Z), HYDROPAC 3257/26 (North Pacific, Midway Islands: early Hawaii, 0130-0501Z), HYDROPAC 3254/26 (South Pacific west of Chile, 0812-1137Z), HYDROPAC 3256/26 (North Pacific, Micronesia to north-east of Hawaii: late Hawaii, 2217-0144Z). The 14-20 Nov windows belong to the 13-19 Nov launch dates. Each contingency window opens as the modeled descent enters its area at about 80 km and closes about one orbit plus 20 min after the first-pass splashdown, so each covers two consecutive passes; the model shows the first.

Sunlight: geometric WGS-84 occultation of the Sun centre with JPL DE440s at 60 s cadence. Shifting T0 keeps the Earth-fixed path and moves the Sun. Cities beyond the template list are added for the Americas, the Pacific and the deorbit regions; the sky chart opens on South Padre Island.

Sources: spacex.com/launches/starship-flight-15 and spacex.com/updates (7 Nov 2026) for the timeline, window, catch description and contingency areas; the Flight 14 model at github.com/exoplanet5/Starship-IFT14 for the plane, zones and ship calibration.

Early Hawaii: Flight 14's as-flown profile re-timed by the 42 s later insertion: deorbit burn 71.0 m/s at T+02:12:42 on orbit 2 (the Early Hawaii Return Check is at T+01:27:46), bank 19.5 deg, splashdown at Flight 14's reported point 25.50 N 155.43 W, 450 km north of Oahu. HYDROPAC 3257/26 is the Flight 14 North Pacific polygon; its window opens at 0130Z, as this descent enters the area at 80 km after a 22:45Z launch, and also covers an orbit-3 descent.

zones.label: Launch · Gulf
zones.desc: Launch hazard area A, Gulf of America, Yucatán Channel and the Caribbean south of Cuba (NAVAREA IV 1080/26, 9 Nov 2026)

zones.label: Launch · area B
zones.desc: Launch hazard area B off Starbase, the Super Heavy return (NAVAREA IV 1080/26, 9 Nov 2026)

zones.label: Indian Ocean · no insertion
zones.desc: Suborbital contingency: no insertion burn, splashdown from the SECO coast (HYDROPAC 3244/26, 7 Nov 2026)

zones.label: N Pacific · early Hawaii
zones.desc: Early-mission contingency: deorbit on orbit 2 (the window also covers orbit 3), splashdown north of Hawaii; the Flight 14 polygon (HYDROPAC 3257/26, 9 Nov 2026)

zones.label: S Pacific · W of Chile
zones.desc: Mid-mission contingency: deorbit on orbit 7 (the window also covers orbit 8), landing several hundred km west of Chile (HYDROPAC 3254/26, 9 Nov 2026)

zones.label: N Pacific · late Hawaii
zones.desc: Late-mission contingency on orbit 16, the pass after the Starbase pass (the window also covers orbit 17): entry from Micronesia to a splashdown north-east of Hawaii (HYDROPAC 3256/26, 9 Nov 2026)

zones.label: Ship entry · Mexico C2
zones.desc: Ship return: entry corridor in the Mexico FIR, surface to unlimited, from the Pacific off Baja California across the peninsula, the Gulf of California and Sonora; the ship is at 72 to 63 km (NOTAM B4288/26, area C2)

zones.label: Ship entry · Mexico C3
zones.desc: Ship return: entry corridor in the Mexico FIR, surface to unlimited, across Chihuahua and Coahuila to the Rio Grande north-west of Laredo; the ship is at 63 to 53 km (NOTAM B4288/26, area C3)

zones.label: Ship catch · Starbase
zones.desc: Ship return: Laguna Madre, Padre Island and the Gulf off Starbase for the final approach and catch; the land corridor is under FAA notices (NAVAREA IV 1081/26, 9 Nov 2026)

events.label: Super Heavy landing burn shutdown and catch
